a: Dirty read sees uncommitted data from another transaction.
A row read twice changes because another transaction committed an update.
A range query returns new rows committed by others between reads.
Read Committed avoids dirty reads; default in many databases.
Repeatable Read keeps row reads stable within a transaction (details vary by engine).
Serializable prevents anomalies by making transactions appear one-by-one.
Optimistic concurrency detects conflicts at commit via versions/ETags.
Pessimistic locking locks rows early to block conflicting writers.
2PC coordinates commit across multiple resources; can block on failures.
Sagas coordinate distributed workflows with compensating transactions.
